title: Adaptive Entitlement Orchestration and Emergency Overdraft Routing PRD
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Customers operating in Dedicated/Private modes run varied traffic patterns across routes and models. Current static quota slices and hard overages either cause unnecessary application failures or surprise invoices. We need an orchestration layer that dynamically composes plan entitlements (per-plan slices, per-route priorities, temporal windows), routes emergency overdraft requests to prioritized debt pools, and emits auditable billing events for reconciliation.
goals: Define a deterministic entitlement matrix that maps plan -> route -> resource (tokens, embeddings, concurrency) with time-windowed overrides
Introduce an emergency overdraft routing mechanism with priority weighting and controlled gracebanding to keep high-priority traffic alive during peaks
Ensure every entitlement decision emits a verifiable billing event and decision metadata for downstream invoice reconciliation and dispute resolution
Provide a canary rollout path for plan-level policy changes and a safe rollback when regressions are detected
non_goals: Replace existing billing engine; we will emit events that the billing backend consumes
Full UI for all matrix edits in phase 1; initial admin UX will be scoped to a console feature flag
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Prefer deterministic decisioning (rule-evaluation tree) over ML-based heuristics for first release to simplify auditability
Use soft-overdraft with token-burn accounting rather than extending hard credit to avoid long-term unpaid liability
Favor lightweight per-tenant in-memory caches for latency-sensitive checks, with periodic reconciliation to the canonical store (eventual consistency vs strict consistency tradeoff)
Emergency overdraft will be funded from prioritized credit buckets (reserved credits) before defaulting to invoiceable overage to reduce billing surprises
acceptance_criteria: Policy definition: Product team can author a plan entitlement matrix encoding per-plan token quotas, per-route priorities, and per-window overrides through a JSON spec

Decision correctness: For a generated test-corpus (1000 synthetic requests spanning routes and windows), entitlement decisions match the expected decisions in 99.9% of cases as validated by the policy simulator
Overdraft routing: When a plan exhausts its quota, the system routes requests to the highest-priority available overdraft bucket and logs the bucket id in the billing event
Graceband enforcement: Soft-overdraft is allowed up to configured threshold per plan; requests beyond graceband are rejected with standardized error code QUOTA_EXCEEDED_SOFT

Billing events: Every request that affects quota (charge, overdraft, rejection) emits a billing event with fields: tenant_id, plan_id, route, model, timestamp, decision_reason, tokens_charged, overdraft_bucket, event_id
Audit trail: Billing events are replayable to reconcile usage and must be storable for 90 days in event-store; sample replay on staging yields matching aggregated invoice totals within 0.01%
Performance: Entitlement decisioning latency p50 <= 6ms and p99 <= 20ms for cold and warmed caches on hosted infra equivalent to m5-large sized control-plane hosts
Rollout safety: Feature flag controlled rollout with canary at 1% tenants, auto-rollback if invoice delta > 2% or error-rate increase > 1.5x over baseline
Console controls: Admins can view active entitlement matrix for a tenant and manually trigger overdraft transfers; UI skeleton exists behind feature flag
Docs & runbook: Ops runbook created with steps for emergency revocation of overdraft buckets and billing dispute flow
metrics_and_success_criteria: Reduction in customer-facing QUOTA_EXCEEDED incidents by 40% for affected tenants in first 30 days
Overdraft invoice adjustments < 0.5% of total overdraft dollars after 60 days
Decision latency impact on p99 API request latency < 5%
Number of disputed bills arising from orchestration decisions < 1 per 10k tenants per month
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (proto): policy schema + simulator + unit tests (owner: PM, ETA: 3w)
Phase 1 (core): decision engine + billing event emitter + staging integration with billing (owner: Eng runtime & billing, ETA: 6w)
Phase 2 (ops): console controls + runbook + RBAC + KMS metadata signing of events (owner: Product & Security, ETA: 4w)
Phase 3 (rollout): canary on 1% tenants -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated checks and manual gating (owner: Growth & Customer Success, ETA: 4w)
Phase 4 (hardening): add per-route concurrency slices and cross-tenant spillover policies (stretch goals)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overdraft used as permanent credit leading to AR issues. Mitigation: require manual approval for overdraft > threshold and flag high consumers for finance review
Risk: Decision engine adds tail latency. Mitigation: aggressive local caching + ephemeral prefetch for high-freq tenants and telemetry to detect regressions
Risk: Billing event mismatch between control-plane and billing backend. Mitigation: idempotent event schema, signed event payloads, and daily reconciliation job with alerts
rollout_criteria: Canary stable for 72h with no invoice delta > 2% and error-rate within threshold
Reconciliation job shows matching aggregates for canary tenants for 2 consecutive days
Support team trained and runbook published
